title: How to Avoid Air Duct Cleaning Scams
h1: How to Avoid Air Duct Cleaning Scams
description: Learn the warning signs of air duct cleaning scams, from too-cheap whole-house offers to fake mold claims, and what a real duct cleaning should include.
quick_answer: Avoid air duct cleaning scams by skipping deals that seem too cheap for a whole house, asking exactly what's included before work starts, refusing high-pressure upsells, and asking to see proof of any problems found. Check the company's California contractor license, read recent reviews and choose a local company with a real address.
body:
How do air duct cleaning scams work?

The most common pattern is the bait and switch. A flyer, robocall or online ad promises whole-house duct cleaning for a price that seems impossibly low. Once the crew arrives, the price climbs: extra charges per vent, a surcharge for the return, then a sudden discovery of mold that needs expensive treatment right away.

Other scams are simpler. The crew runs a shop vacuum over the vent covers, spends an hour in the house and leaves the ducts as dirty as they were. You pay for a service that never really happened.

What are the warning signs?

  • Prices that seem too good to be true. A proper cleaning takes specialized equipment and several hours. Very low whole-house offers are usually a way to get in the door.
  • Vague scope. If they can't tell you how many vents are included or what equipment they use, be careful.
  • Sudden mold claims. Some crews show photos that may not even be from your home. Ask to see the spot yourself.
  • High-pressure upsells. Being told you must buy sanitizing, coatings or new equipment today is a red flag.
  • No local address. Companies that only have a phone number and change names often are hard to hold accountable.
  • Unsolicited calls. Robocalls offering duct cleaning are a common starting point for these schemes.

What does a real duct cleaning include?

Knowing what proper work looks like makes it easier to spot a shortcut. A legitimate duct cleaning includes:

  1. An inspection of the system before work starts, with findings explained
  2. A powerful vacuum connected to the duct system to keep it under negative pressure
  3. Brushes, air whips or similar tools run through each supply and return line
  4. Cleaning of registers, grilles and the return plenum
  5. A look at the blower and coil area, with recommendations if they need cleaning
  6. Before and after photos or a camera view on request

The job usually takes several hours for a typical house. Our air duct cleaning service follows these steps, and we're happy to walk you through them before we start.

How should you check out a duct cleaning company?

A few minutes of research can save you money and frustration:

  • Look up the company's contractor license on the California Contractors State License Board website and confirm it's active
  • Read recent reviews and look for comments about surprise charges
  • Ask for a written estimate that lists what's included
  • Ask whether they use negative-pressure equipment, and what kind
  • Ask how they handle findings like mold or damaged ducts, and whether you can see them

We hold California Contractor License #1036543 and work out of our office in Kearny Mesa. We're a family-owned company serving San Diego County and Orange County.

What should you do if a crew claims they found mold?

Don't agree to anything on the spot. Ask to see the area yourself, take your own photos and ask what's causing the moisture. Mold in ducts usually has a reason, such as a leaky duct, a clogged drain or condensation around the coil, and treating the growth without fixing the cause won't solve anything.

You're always free to get a second opinion before paying for mold treatment. A trustworthy company will understand.

What questions should you ask before booking?

Have these ready when you call for a quote:

  • Is the price for the whole house, or per vent?
  • Are the return ducts and the return plenum included?
  • What equipment will you use, and will the system be under negative pressure?
  • How long will the job take?
  • Will you show me photos or camera footage of the ducts?

Clear, direct answers are a good sign. Dodging the questions or changing the subject to a limited-time deal is not.

Is duct cleaning ever worth it?

Yes. Duct cleaning is useful after remodeling, rodent problems, wildfire smoke, or when you can see dust and debris inside the system. The key is paying for an actual cleaning done with the right equipment rather than a cheap visit that just moves dust around.
faqs: Why are some duct cleaning offers so cheap?
Very low whole-house prices are often a way to get into your home and upsell. The final bill may include per-vent charges, add-ons or mold treatment that weren't mentioned in the ad.
How long should a real duct cleaning take?
A typical home takes several hours. A crew that finishes a whole house in under an hour is unlikely to have cleaned the ducts properly.
How can I verify a duct cleaning company's license?
Use the license lookup on the California Contractors State License Board website. Enter the license number and confirm the name matches and the license is active.
Should I pay up front for duct cleaning?
Be cautious about paying the full amount before the work is done. Ask about payment terms when you get your estimate, and get them in writing.
